reference_guided_design.owner_intent: The owner wants each user to be able to reshape their workbench with the embedded AI using a description, a selected screenshot or a reference URL, for example a page they found on Mobbin or Dribbble. A request may cover the whole workbench, one widget or an element inside it.
reference_guided_design.visual_reference: Interpret the selected reference for its hierarchy, spacing, typography and composition. Create an editable ScopeHub layout rendered by the desktop application. Use the available page or image capabilities and the user's chosen model route and disclosure scope. If a page cannot be read, accept a screenshot the user can provide. If image input is unavailable, a description still works as a design input.
reference_guided_design.composition: Let users combine fields, images, text, repeated cards or rows, groups and containers into a new view. Bind the result to records and actions from services available to that user. Preserve item identity, attribution and links when changing presentation. New records use the same arrangement and grouping on refresh.
reference_guided_design.editing_scope: Apply manual and AI edits to the same saved workbench. A local edit targets the selected part and preserves neighboring views. A whole-workbench edit may rearrange or replace them together. Both support preview, undo and further manual edits. The application retains ownership of global settings, credentials and native permission dialogs.

illustrative_acceptance.given: A synthetic, authorized information feed supplies item IDs, headlines, source attribution, publication times and an optional image. The initial workbench shows a Top News list beside another widget.
illustrative_acceptance.actions: Restyle only the list as image cards. Keep a text card for an item with no image. Split the same feed into two independently placed views, for example today's and earlier headlines using the displayed time zone. Then use a reference to rearrange the whole workbench.
illustrative_acceptance.observations_to_verify: The local edit preserves the neighboring widget. Every original item appears once across the two time groups with its source, time and link intact. A new matching item appears under the same rule on refresh. Undo restores the prior presentation and retains the data. Saving and reopening restores the revised composition and rechecks its bindings.

reference_guided_design.status: Owner intent and a proposed acceptance scenario. The news example assumes an independently available information service. Desktop reference ingestion, model interpretation and feed rendering still require implementation and validation.

current_scope.v1: The contract specifies one main instrument chart and declarative customization. ScopeHub already saves and restores named single-chart layouts. The chart adapter renders price first, volume second, and indicator series as price overlays or in separate panes appended after volume.
current_scope.M2-012: Planned current-contract work composes built-in widgets around the single main chart, starting with an inspection table. It covers compatible authorized local and API bindings, linked or independent selections, arrangement and restore.
current_scope.M2-003: Planned later work evaluates isolated user-authored panels only when a concrete need exceeds declarative bindings. Runtime execution would require a separate decision.

recommendations.starting_points: Start with a TradingView-inspired default and offer an optional genuinely blank workspace with no views or chart. From either starting point, users can ask the embedded AI to design the workspace and continue editing by hand or by AI. A workspace menu stays reachable from an empty layout so the user can add a view or restore the default.
recommendations.workspace: Use OpenBB Workspace as the reference for adding, arranging and resizing built-in views such as charts and inspection tables. Use relative sizes so layouts adapt to window changes, and offer snap or docking as optional placement aids. Bind each view to compatible authorized data, with the option to follow the active selection or pin its own.
recommendations.chart: A chart contains series such as candles, volume and computed indicators. Overlay compatible series in an existing pane or place them in an ordered pane, including between candles and volume. Panes align on a compatible time axis and have independent value scales and units. Consider independent charts when a specific workflow needs a separate symbol, time basis or viewport. For example, a daily K-line chart and an intraday view can follow the same instrument while retaining different time scales. Daily bars and opening or closing auction records alone cannot supply a continuous intraday price series.
recommendations.appearance: Let users adjust typography, colors, line styles, spacing and panel proportions per workspace. Keep the source, data freshness and action confirmations accessible across themes and custom layouts.
recommendations.editing_and_recovery: Use one versioned declarative layout for manual and AI edits through the shared operation registry. Address views, panes and series by stable IDs and store pane order explicitly. An AI request to change one pane should preserve unrelated choices. Preview the affected parts and allow the user to undo an applied edit. Save named layouts and recover the last committed revision after interruption. On reopen, recheck source grants and preserve a view's place if its data is unavailable.
recommendations.boundaries: Keep source grants separate from layout references. Attach immutable indicator results by version so placement and styling never rewrite computed values. Render with built-in components and prohibit generated code in the main WebView.

observed_library_probe.setup: Headless Chromium with lightweight-charts 5.2.1 and 65 synthetic one-minute bars. The visible logical range was 18..48.
observed_library_probe.result: A test line moved from below volume to between price and volume. Its pane measured 86 px. Price and volume values and the logical range stayed the same. Removing the line restored the original price and volume order.
observed_library_probe.scope: Chart library only. Native UI, model interaction and persistence still require product validation.

first_proposed_demonstration: With a frozen desktop sample, use manual controls and an embedded AI request to preview and place the same existing computed indicator between candles and volume. Resize its pane, undo the resize and placement, then reapply, save the named layout and reopen it. Check that order and size restore and that values, symbol selections, visible range and source authorization stay the same throughout.
open_release_scope: The owner still needs to decide whether the first release should include ordered pane editing, AI-assisted design from scratch or a genuinely blank start with chart-free saved layouts. The current V1 contract specifies a single main chart.
